concepts.title: Print Culture and Social Reform Debates

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Print Culture and Social Reform Debates' refers to.
questions.a: The arrival of inexpensive printed materials like newspapers and tracts enabled public discussion on societal practices in regional vernaculars.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Print Culture and Social Reform Debates'.
questions.a: Mass printing allowed common people to debate and participate in social reform.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Print Culture and Social Reform Debates' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Working Towards Change (source: hess207.txt lines 35-65)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Abolition of Sati' refers to.
questions.a: The eradication of the practice of burning widows on their deceased husbands pyres, accomplished through arguments rooted in ancient scriptures.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Abolition of Sati'.
questions.a: Raja Rammohun Roy demonstrated that ancient texts did not support self-immolation of widows.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Abolition of Sati' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Changing the lives of widows (source: hess207.txt lines 66-105)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Widow Remarriage Reform Movement' refers to.
questions.a: Efforts by social reformers to secure legal approval and social acceptance for widows to marry again.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Widow Remarriage Reform Movement'.
questions.a: Ishwarchandra Vidyasagar utilized ancient texts to support widow remarriage, leading to the law of 1856.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Widow Remarriage Reform Movement' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Changing the lives of widows (source: hess207.txt lines 106-140)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Promoting Female Education' refers to.
questions.a: The establishment of formal educational institutions for young women despite traditional social fears and domestic restrictions.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Promoting Female Education'.
questions.a: Reformers established schools for girls to improve womens position despite orthodox fears of social corruption.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Promoting Female Education' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Girls begin going to school (source: hess207.txt lines 141-190)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Women Reformers and Feminist Literature' refers to.
questions.a: Literary works and institutions created directly by women to critique patriarchal structures and promote female empowerment.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Women Reformers and Feminist Literature'.
questions.a: Educated women authored critical texts and founded institutions to support womens independence.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Women Reformers and Feminist Literature' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Women write about women (source: hess207.txt lines 191-240)

questions.q: Calculate the age difference between male and female minimum legal marriage ages. Use the method 'Child Marriage Restraint Legislation'. Work with: female_min_age = 50, male_min_age = 1500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of age_difference.
questions.a: 1450 years

questions.q: Find the difference between male and female age limits in child marriage laws. Use the method 'Child Marriage Restraint Legislation'. Work with: female_min_age = 10, male_min_age = 1500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of age_difference.
questions.a: 1490 years

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Child Marriage Restraint Legislation' refers to.
questions.a: Statutory provisions establishing minimum legal age thresholds for marriage to protect children from early marriage.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Child Marriage Restraint Legislation'.
questions.a: The 1929 Act set legal minimum marriage ages for males and females to prevent child marriage.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Child Marriage Restraint Legislation', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: age_difference = male_min_age - female_min_age

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Caste Reform and Social Mobility' refers to.
questions.a: Efforts by reform societies and marginalized groups to challenge caste hierarchies and access new urban employment.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Caste Reform and Social Mobility'.
questions.a: Industrial growth and urban expansion offered low-caste individuals alternatives to traditional village servitude.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Caste Reform and Social Mobility' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Caste and Social Reform (source: hess207.txt lines 266-320)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Non-Brahman Equality Movements' refers to.
questions.a: Social and spiritual movements organized within marginalized communities to promote self-respect and social parity.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Non-Brahman Equality Movements'.
questions.a: Non-Brahman leaders established regional movements to instil self-esteem and reject caste hierarchies.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Non-Brahman Equality Movements' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Demands for equality and justice (source: hess207.txt lines 321-360)

concepts.title: Radical Caste Critiques Phule and Periyar

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Radical Caste Critiques Phule and Periyar' refers to.
questions.a: Ideological attacks on Brahmanical supremacy proposing that indigenous populations were subjugated by non-native settlers.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Radical Caste Critiques Phule and Periyar'.
questions.a: Phule and Periyar rejected elite claims to superiority and built movements for indigenous self-respect.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Radical Caste Critiques Phule and Periyar' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Gulamgiri (source: hess207.txt lines 361-415)

concepts.title: Temple Entry Movement and Dalit Assertion

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Temple Entry Movement and Dalit Assertion' refers to.
questions.a: Sustained public campaigns organized by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar to claim access to sacred spaces and public water sources for untouchables.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Temple Entry Movement and Dalit Assertion'.
questions.a: Ambedkar led temple entry Satyagrahas to expose entrenched caste prejudice and assert human dignity.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Temple Entry Movement and Dalit Assertion' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Who could enter temples? (source: hess207.txt lines 416-449)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Nineteenth-Century Reform Organizations' refers to.
questions.a: Formal societies established across India to promote rational thought, education, and social reform while eliminating superstitious practices.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Nineteenth-Century Reform Organizations'.
questions.a: Associations like Brahmo Samaj, Prarthana Samaj, and Aligarh Movement sought comprehensive social and religious renewal.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Nineteenth-Century Reform Organizations' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Organising for reform (source: hess207.txt lines 491-560)
